The 24-character domestic RIB embedded in the CI IBAN contains a five-character bank code, five-character branch code, twelve-character account number, and two-character RIB key. These components remain useful for account validation and local-bank reconciliation.
BIC is required as the canonical cross-provider bank-mapping key. Adaptive Gateway maps it to each provider's proprietary bank ID; it must not expose those provider IDs as customer input.

info.title: Default module
info.description:
The Axiym canonical payment model: a thin, ISO 20022-aligned settlement
instruction. Provider-neutral by design.

Design boundary:
- The canonical Payment carries ISO-anchored settlement fields plus a small
  set of deliberate AML/KYB identity extensions that have a proven consumer.
- Stable party and account data is owned by registry services; the payment
  carries a snapshot referenced by id, not a full CDD record.
- What must be present for a given operation, corridor, and provider is
  resolved by a separate requirements engine, not encoded as schema
  `required`.
- Non-canonical, corridor- or compliance-specific data is materialized into
  governed extension blocks under `complementaryInfo`
  (`corridorRequirements`, `regulatoryMetadata`).
- Provider adapters translate the resulting envelope into the provider
  payload; provider-specific fields never enter this schema.

Multi-leg operations (e.g. an on-chain funding leg plus a fiat payout leg)
are modeled as separate Payment documents correlated by a shared
`endToEndId`, each with its own UETR. Cross-currency conversion, where
performed by a provider, is not modeled here.

Coverage is extended as concrete corridor and provider requirements arise;
not all corridors are represented yet.

Payment Status Code.description: ISO 20022 ExternalPaymentTransactionStatus1Code. Used at transaction level (TxSts) in pacs.002 / pain.002. Codes below are the stable subset relevant to credit transfer lifecycle; additional codes exist in the external code set for direct debits and cancellation flows. ACTC (AcceptedTechnicalValidation) — syntactic and schema validation passed. ACCP (AcceptedCustomerProfile) — preceding customer profile check passed. ACSP (AcceptedSettlementInProcess) — accepted, settlement in progress. ACWC (AcceptedWithChange) — accepted with a modification (e.g. date shift). ACWP (AcceptedWithoutPosting) — accepted but not yet posted to beneficiary. ACSC (AcceptedSettlementCompleted) — debtor side settlement completed (funds left debtor). ACCC (AcceptedSettlementCompletedCreditorAccount) — creditor account credited (terminal success). ACFC (AcceptedFundsChecked) — preceding check of available funds passed. PDNG (Pending) — awaiting further processing (compliance review, SCA, cut-off, etc.). RJCT (Rejected) — terminal failure. CANC (Cancelled) — cancelled by debtor or agent (via camt.055/camt.056 request).

clearingSystemMemberId.description: Member ID (routing number, sort code, IFSC, BSB, etc.) within the clearing system identified by clearingSystem. Maps to ISO 20022 ClrSysMmbId/MmbId.

clearingSystemCode.description: Clearing system code from ISO 20022 ExternalClearingSystemIdentification1Code (e.g. USABA, GBDSC, DEBLZ, INFSC, AUBSB). Qualifies clearingSystemMemberId. Maps to ISO ClrSysId/Cd.

name.description: Full name of the financial institution.

address.description: Postal address of the financial institution. Maps to ISO 20022 PstlAdr on BranchAndFinancialInstitutionIdentification. The address country identifies where the institution is located.

Identification Code.description: Standard code representing the type of identification, based on ISO 20022 External Code Sets. TXID (Tax Identification Number) — unique number assigned by a government tax authority. VATN (VAT Number) — Value Added Tax registration number, widely used in the EU. NIDN (National Identity Number) — unique number issued by a national authority to identify a citizen. CCPT (Passport Number) — unique number of a government-issued travel document. DRLC (Driver's License Number) — identification number on a motor vehicle permit. ARNU (Alien Registration Number) — number assigned to a foreign national by a government immigration authority. IDCD (Identity Card Number) — unique number of a government-issued national identity card. CUST (Customer Number) — internal identification number assigned to a customer by a financial institution. SOCS (Social Security Number) — number issued to track individuals for social security purposes. LEIC (Legal Entity Identifier Code) — unique 20-character alphanumeric code per ISO 17442 for identifying legal entities. CINC (Certificate of Incorporation Number) — company registration number assigned by a corporate registry upon incorporation; the primary official identifier of a legal entity in many jurisdictions.

Status History Entry.description: Single status transition event. Equivalent to one OriginalTransactionReference/TxInfAndSts block in a pacs.002 / pain.002 message.

status.description: Status at this point in the lifecycle.

timestamp.description: Moment the status was observed or reported (ISO 8601, UTC preferred). Maps to the CreDtTm of the corresponding pacs.002 Group Header for externally reported events.

reasonCode.description: ISO 20022 StatusReasonCode from External Code Set ExternalStatusReason1Code (e.g. G000 = 'Accepted, no change', AM04 = 'InsufficientFunds', AC01 = 'IncorrectAccountNumber'). Maps to StsRsnInf/Rsn/Cd in pacs.002.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of the status. Maps to StsRsnInf/AddtlInf in pacs.002 (max 105 chars per occurrence, up to 3 occurrences in ISO 20022).

localReference.description: Optional local reference issued by the party reporting this status (e.g. clearing system reference, RTGS ID, local switch transaction ID). Maps to AcctSvcrRef or ClrSysRef depending on the reporting actor.

reportingAgent.description: Optional BIC of the agent that generated this status event. Useful when the payment traverses multiple agents each emitting pacs.002. Maps to InstgAgt in the pacs.002 Group Header.

Execution Status.description: Lifecycle status of the payment, tracked by the initiating or servicing party. Aligned with ISO 20022 ExternalPaymentTransactionStatus1Code (used in pacs.002 TxSts and pain.002 TxInfAndSts/TxSts). For batch / group level, use the same codes at GrpSts or PmtInfSts.

statusHistory.description: Ordered history of status transitions. Each entry represents one pacs.002 / pain.002 status event. Must be sorted by timestamp ascending; currentStatus must equal the last entry's status.

External References.description: References assigned to the transaction by external systems outside the initiating party's domain. All fields are optional and populated as the payment traverses the chain.

pspReference.description: Reference assigned by an intermediary PSP (Payment Service Provider). No ISO 20022 direct equivalent; typically conveyed in InstructionId on the PSP's leg or in ClearingSystemReference.

bankReference.description: Reference assigned by a bank in the chain (debtor agent, intermediary agent, or creditor agent). Maps to ISO 20022 TxId (TransactionIdentification) or AccountServicerReference.

txHash.description: On-chain transaction hash when settlement occurs via a public or permissioned blockchain network. Not part of ISO 20022; used in conjunction with settlementMethod = ON_CHAIN and Money.networkIdentifier.

Tracking.description: End-to-end transaction tracking identifiers. The UETR is the primary correlation key across ISO 20022 messages (pacs.008, pacs.009, pacs.002, pacs.004, pacs.028) and SWIFT MT Field 121. External references capture identifiers assigned by other actors in the chain (PSPs, banks, blockchain).

uetr.description: Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference. UUID v4 assigned by the debtor agent (first instructing party). Immutable across the entire payment chain. Maps to ISO 20022 PmtId/UETR and SWIFT Field 121 in Block 3. Mandatory in CBPR+ since Nov 2018.

externalReferences.description: References assigned by counterparties or external systems. Not part of UETR tracking but useful for reconciliation.

Currency Code.description: ISO 4217 currency code or crypto asset ticker. USD (US Dollar) — fiat currency of the United States. EUR (Euro) — fiat currency of the Eurozone. GBP (British Pound Sterling) — fiat currency of the United Kingdom. USDT (Tether) — USD-pegged stablecoin. Always specify networkIdentifier to identify the chain (e.g. ERC20, TRON, BSC). USDC (USD Coin) — USD-pegged stablecoin. Always specify networkIdentifier to identify the chain (e.g. ERC20, BSC, SOL). BTC (Bitcoin) — native crypto asset of the Bitcoin network. networkIdentifier not required. ETH (Ethereum) — native asset of the Ethereum network. networkIdentifier not required for native ETH transfers. The currency list above is documentation only; this field is a free-form string (ISO 4217 fiat code or crypto/stablecoin ticker), so corridor currencies such as INR, AED, and BDT are accepted without a schema change.

amount.description: Amount as a string, up to 18 digits and up to 2 decimal places.

networkIdentifier.description: Blockchain network identifier. Required when currency is USDT or USDC (e.g. ERC20, TRON, BSC, SOL). Not required for BTC or ETH. Omit for fiat currencies.

Complementary Info.description: Extended metadata for corridor-specific requirements, regulatory compliance, and execution context. Structure is flexible and defined per integration profile.

corridorRequirements.description: Corridor-specific mandatory fields not covered by the core schema (e.g. local regulatory fields).

regulatoryMetadata.description: AML/CFT and regulatory reporting data (e.g. FATF Travel Rule fields, sanctions screening results, risk scores).

executionMetadata.description: Operational metadata for execution tracking (e.g. PSP-B reference, execution timestamp, hold reason, retry count).

Charges Information.description: Fee bearing and charge amount details.

chargeBearer.description: Who bears the transaction charges. DEBT (Debtor) — Sender pays all fees. CRED (Creditor) — Recipient pays all fees. SHAR (Shared) — Fees shared between sender and recipient. Standard for SWIFT. SLEV (Service Level) — Charge bearing as agreed in the applicable service level.

chargeAmount.description: Amount and currency of the charges applied.

Remittance Information.description: Information about the underlying transaction or invoice.

unstructured.description: Free-text remittance reference shown to the recipient (ISO RmtInf/Ustrd).

structured.description: Structured remittance reference, typically for B2B payments.

Payment Type Information.description: Scheme-level routing hints for the payment (ISO 20022 PmtTpInf).

localInstrument.description: Local instrument or scheme code specific to the destination market.

Branch Identification.description: Branch of a financial institution, used where the FI identification does not identify the branch (e.g. JP bank code + branch code, LK, HK). Maps to ISO 20022 BranchData (BranchIdentification).

id.description: Branch identifier (ISO Id). Local branch code where distinct from the clearing-system member id.

Agent.description: Financial institution (bank or payment provider) acting as agent for a party.

branchIdentification.description: Optional branch identifier for institutions that expose bank and branch as separate identifiers. Maps to ISO 20022 BranchIdentification.

Proxy.description: Alternative proxy identifier for an account (used in instant payment schemes).

type.description: Type of proxy identifier. MSISDN (Mobile Number) — mobile phone number in international format. EMAIL (Email Address) — email address registered to the account. NATIONAL_ID (National ID) — national identity number registered to the account. OTHER — any other proxy identifier type.

Account Identifier Type.description: The identifier scheme used to interpret accountId. IBAN (International Bank Account Number) — standard international bank account identifier. BBAN (Basic Bank Account Number) — local format bank account number without country code. WALLET (Crypto/Digital Wallet Address) — on-chain or digital wallet public address. CUSTODIAL_ID (Custodial ID) — internal identifier in a centralized exchange or custody platform. CASH — represents a cash delivery payout rather than a traditional account. accountId is not required. Used for agent banking and cash-out corridors. INTERNAL (Internal/Virtual Account) — internal or virtual account within a platform. OTHER — any other account type not covered above.

accountId.description: Account number, IBAN, or wallet address.

accountType.description: Functional type of the account (current/savings). Maps to ISO 20022 CashAccount/Tp/Cd. Optional; conditionally required by certain providers and corridors (e.g. telegraphic transfers).

proxy.description: Alternative account identifier (e.g. phone number, email). Primarily used for creditor accounts.

Identification.description: Identity document details for a party.

identificationId.description: Document number (e.g. passport number, tax ID).

issuerCountry.description: Country that issued the identification document.

issuingDate.description: Date the identification was issued (YYYY-MM-DD). Compliance/KYB extension beyond ISO 20022 payment scope. Optional; requiredness applied by corridor rules.

expiryDate.description: Date the identification expires (YYYY-MM-DD). Compliance/KYB extension beyond ISO 20022 payment scope; supports document-validity checks. Optional; requiredness applied by corridor rules.

Contact.description: Party contact details. Maps to ISO 20022 ContactDetails (CtctDtls): emailAddress = EmailAdr, phoneNumber = PhneNb, mobileNumber = MobNb, urlAddress = URLAdr. All fields optional at the model level; requiredness (e.g. mobileNumber for some corridors) is applied by corridor rules, not the base schema.

emailAddress.description: Email address. Maps to ISO 20022 EmailAdr.

phoneNumber.description: Phone number in international format. Maps to ISO 20022 PhneNb.

mobileNumber.description: Mobile number in international format. Maps to ISO 20022 MobNb.

urlAddress.description: Website or URL. Maps to ISO 20022 URLAdr.

Place Of Birth.description: Place of birth of an individual. Maps to ISO 20022 DateAndPlaceOfBirth (paired with dateOfBirth): city = CityOfBirth, province = PrvcOfBirth, country = CtryOfBirth. Recognized by FATF Recommendation 16 as an originator-identification option. Optional; requiredness applied by corridor rules.

province.description: Province or region of birth (ISO PrvcOfBirth).

name.description: Full name or registered business name.

partyType.description: Type of party. INDIVIDUAL — a natural person. dateOfBirth and personal identification are expected. BUSINESS — a registered legal entity. LEIC or TXID are the preferred identification types.

countryOfResidence.description: Country of residence for individuals, or country of registration for businesses.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD). Required for individuals in most corridors.

placeOfBirth.description: Place of birth (ISO 20022 DateAndPlaceOfBirth, paired with dateOfBirth). Optional; requiredness applied by corridor rules.

contact.description: Party contact details (ISO 20022 ContactDetails). Optional at the model level; requiredness (e.g. mobileNumber for some corridors) is applied by corridor rules.

Payment Party.description: A party (debtor or creditor) in the payment, including their account and agent.

settlementMethod.description: Settlement method used across financial institutions. CLEARING (Traditional Clearing) — standard batch clearing through an interbank clearing system (e.g. ACH, BACS, SEPA Credit Transfer). Typically settles in 1-3 business days. INSTANT (Instant Payment) — real-time settlement through an instant payment scheme (e.g. SEPA Instant, UK Faster Payments, UPI, PIX). Typically settles within seconds. INTERNAL — settlement within the same platform or institution without an external clearing system. ON_CHAIN (Blockchain) — settlement directly on a distributed ledger network (e.g. Ethereum, Tron, Solana). Used for crypto asset transfers. Proprietary Axiym extension. OTHER — any other settlement method.

priority.description: Urgency of payment processing. NORMAL — standard processing queue, subject to normal cut-off times and SLAs. HIGH — elevated priority, placed ahead of NORMAL payments. May incur additional fees. URGENT — immediate or near-immediate execution required. Typically maps to RTGS for fiat or high-gas-price transactions for crypto.

serviceLevel.description: ISO 20022 or proprietary service level code (e.g. SEPA, SWFT, URGP).

originCountry.description: Country from which the payment originates. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

destinationCountry.description: Country to which the payment is being sent. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

endToEndId.description: End-to-end identifier, mandatory for payment tracking.

initiatingPartyId.description: Identifier of the party that submitted the payment instruction on the debtor's mandate. Maps to ISO 20022 InitiatingParty (InitgPty, pain.001). The initiating party may differ from any agent in the chain: it is the platform originating the instruction, not an account-servicing institution. System-assigned; the value resolves to the Axiym legal entity (registered name and LEI available on request).

instructedAmount.description: Amount and currency instructed by the debtor.

settledAmount.description: Amount and currency actually settled. Maps to ISO 20022 InterbankSettlementAmount (IntrBkSttlmAmt). System-populated after settlement; may differ from instructedAmount under FX or charges. Read-only.

paymentId.description: Unique transaction ID assigned by the initiating party.

tracking.description: End-to-end payment tracking identifiers. Maps to ISO 20022 PmtId/UETR (pacs.008/pacs.009) and SWIFT gpi Field 121.

ultimateDebtor.description: The ultimate originator of the funds when it differs from the debtor. When the debtor is the actual originator, it may mirror the debtor party details.

ultimateCreditor.description: The ultimate beneficiary of the funds when it differs from the creditor. When the creditor is the actual beneficiary, it may mirror the creditor party details.

purpose.description: ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose1Code — the underlying reason for the payment (Purp). Closed set mirrored from the axiym.payment.Purpose proto enum.

executionStatus.description: Current and historical lifecycle status of the payment. Uses ISO 20022 PaymentTransactionStatus codes (pacs.002 / pain.002).

Account Type.description: Functional type of the cash account (the account product held at the servicing institution), based on ISO 20022 ExternalCashAccountType1Code. CACC (Current) — account used to post debits and credits when no specific account has been nominated; the default for business/checking accounts. SVGS (Savings) — account used for savings. OTHR (Other) — account type not covered by the listed codes. Distinct from accountIdentifierType, which describes the format of the account identifier (IBAN, BBAN, ...), not the account product. Some providers require this for telegraphic transfers; requiredness is corridor/provider-specific and enforced in the rules layer.

info.title: Complementary Info
info.description:
Complementary Info defines structured extension fields for information needed
in a particular payment context but not native to every payment. It does not
change the canonical Payment model.

It separates three concerns:
- `corridorRequirements` holds payment, party, or account facts that remain
  meaningful if the payout provider changes.
- `regulatoryMetadata` holds supplementary information used for AML, CFT,
  KYB, or other regulatory processing.
- `executionMetadata` identifies the payout provider selected by Axiym.

Country and provider rules determine which fields are required. Provider API
field names, proprietary codes, routing state, and lifecycle references remain
in provider integrations rather than in Complementary Info.

Complementary Info.description: Structured payment context stored under payment.complementaryInfo. It adds information needed for a particular corridor, regulatory context, or execution route without changing the core Payment instruction. Values are grouped by their meaning and lifecycle, not by the rule source that made them required.

corridorRequirements.description: Non-canonical facts about the payment, parties, or accounts that remain true if the payout provider changes. Country and provider rules may both require these facts, but provider-required does not mean provider-owned.

regulatoryMetadata.description: Supplementary party and transaction information used for AML, CFT, KYB, and regulatory processing.

executionMetadata.description: Identifies the selected payout provider. Provider lifecycle references, routing state, attempts, and institution mappings remain in their owning execution systems rather than in the payment's complementary information.

Corridor Requirements.description: Non-canonical input facts needed to prepare a payment. These values describe the payment or its parties and remain meaningful across provider changes. A provider may require a value globally even though the canonical extension object is named corridorRequirements.

partyRelationships.description: Directional relationships between canonical payment parties that are not represented by ISO payment roles.

supportingDocuments.description: References to transaction evidence. Document files remain outside the payment body.

profileData.description: Non-canonical semantic payment facts that have not yet been promoted to explicit reusable fields. Do not store provider field names, provider enum codes, fixed adapter values, or system-generated execution state here.

Payment Party Relationships.description: Business context between canonical payment parties. These relationships describe why the parties transact; they are distinct from regulatory relationships such as UBO ownership.

creditorToDebtor.description: The creditor's relationship to the debtor. For example, the creditor may be the debtor's supplier, contractor, subsidiary, or service provider.

Business Relationship.description: A provider-neutral classification of a business relationship between payment parties.

description.description: Additional relationship context when the type alone is insufficient, particularly when type is OTHER.

Business Relationship Type.description: Provider-neutral business relationship type. Provider adapters translate this value to provider-specific codes.

Supporting Document Reference.description: Reference to evidence stored and governed by a document service.

documentId.description: Stable reference to the externally stored document.

documentVersion.description: Referenced document version where the document service supports versioning.

description.description: Short explanation of how the document supports the payment.

Regulatory Metadata.description: AML, CFT, KYB, and related regulatory data outside the thin ISO payment instruction.

sourceOfFunds.description: Classification and evidence for the transaction's source of funds.

partySupplementaryData.description: Additional attributes for canonical payment parties, keyed by payment role so requirements can target an unambiguous path.

relatedPartyData.description: Regulatory relationships keyed first by the canonical payment party and then by relationship type. A UBO is a related party, not an ultimate payment party.

complianceReferences.description: References to system-generated compliance assessments. Detailed screening evidence remains in the owning compliance service.

profileData.description: Regulatory values that have not been promoted to reusable fields. Their expected shape is defined by the applicable requirements.

Source of Funds.description: A source-of-funds classification independent of any provider's code list.

code.description: Source-of-funds value in the named scheme.

scheme.description: Classification scheme that defines the code.

description.description: Free-text explanation where the classification needs additional context.

Party Supplementary Data By Role.description: Supplementary data grouped by canonical payment role. A country or provider rule can require a field for one role without applying it to the others.

Party Supplementary Data.description: Non-canonical attributes for one existing payment party. Its role is established by the containing property.

partyProfileId.description: Reference to the versioned party profile in the owning registry.

industry.description: Business industry classification when required for regulatory or provider processing.

nationalities.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 nationality codes required by the selected profile.

designation.description: Role, occupation, or designation required by the selected regulatory or provider profile.

Industry Classification.description: Industry value qualified by its classification scheme.

code.description: Industry code in the selected scheme.

description.description: Human-readable description of the classified activity.

Related Party Data By Role.description: Related-party information grouped by the canonical payment party to which the relationship applies.

Related Parties For Payment Role.description: Related parties grouped by relationship type. The containing payment-role property identifies which canonical party they relate to.

Related Party.description: Data about an individual related to a canonical payment party. The containing properties establish both the payment role and relationship type.

partyProfileId.description: Reference to the related party in the owning registry when one is available.

givenName.description: Given name of the related individual.

middleName.description: Middle name of the related individual.

familyName.description: Family name of the related individual.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format.

designation.description: Role, occupation, or designation required by the selected regulatory or provider profile.

ownershipPercentage.description: Direct or attributed ownership percentage when applicable.

Related Party Address.description: Postal address of a related party, aligned with the canonical Party address vocabulary.

Related Party Identification.description: Identification of a related party, aligned with the canonical Party identification vocabulary.

Related Party Contact.description: Contact details for a related party.

Compliance Reference.description: Reference to an assessment owned by a compliance system.

assessmentId.description: Identifier of the assessment in its owning service.

status.description: Decision state exposed to payment processing.

assessedAt.description: Time at which the referenced assessment was completed.

Execution Metadata.description: Identifies the payout provider selected by Axiym. Other execution state remains in the owning orchestration and provider-integration systems.

providerId.description: Axiym identifier of the selected payout provider.
